column2: The 12 Domains of Agentic AI Engineering
Complete coverage of all major Agentic AI architectural domains with scope, key concepts, and related domains

column4: Description & Scope

The foundational structural design controlling how autonomous agents perceive input, reason about it, execute actions, and learn from outcomes. Covers single-agent cognitive architectures, the Perception-Reasoning-Action (PRA) loop, and the 8 canonical patterns that dominate production systems: ReAct (Reasoning + Acting), Reflexion (self-evaluation), Plan-and-Execute, and Tool-Use agents. Also covers reasoning patterns including Chain-of-Thought (CoT), Tree of Thoughts (ToT), and Graph of Thoughts (GoT).
column5: PRA Loop, ReAct, Reflexion, Plan-and-Execute, CoT, ToT, GoT, Tool-Use, Adaptive Reasoning Orchestrator, Single vs Multi-Agent patterns

column4: The study and engineering of systems where multiple specialized agents collaborate, compete, or coordinate to accomplish tasks no single agent could handle alone. Covers three primary topologies: Leader-Worker (Orchestrator-Workers), Sequential Pipeline, and Peer Collaboration. Includes agent communication protocols (MCP, A2A, ANP, ACP), agent discovery, task decomposition strategies, and the Society of Minds pattern.
column5: Leader-Worker, Sequential Pipeline, Peer Collaboration, AutoGen, CrewAI, LangGraph, Agent Cards, Task Objects, Hierarchical vs Flat architectures

column4: The coordination layer that manages how agents are instantiated, scheduled, executed, and monitored across complex workflows. Covers workflow design patterns, state machine-based orchestration (LangGraph), human-in-the-loop integration, conditional branching, parallel execution, error handling with retry/fallback logic, and dynamic task routing. Includes orchestration at scale: handling hundreds of concurrent agents.
column5: LangGraph, State Machines, Human-in-the-Loop (HITL), Workflow DAGs, Conditional Routing, Parallel Execution, Retry Logic, Dynamic Task Assignment

column4: The architectural layer that enables agents to store, retrieve, and utilize information across time horizons. Covers three memory layers: Short-term (context window, session state), Long-term (vector databases, persistent storage), and the three-layer agent memory model: Episodic (events/experiences), Semantic (facts/concepts/relationships), and Procedural (skills/processes). Includes memory consolidation, retrieval-augmented memory, and forgetting mechanisms.
column5: Vector DBs (Pinecone, Weaviate, Qdrant), Redis, Episodic Memory, Semantic Memory, Procedural Memory, Context Windows, Memory Consolidation, Knowledge Graphs

column4: The cognitive capabilities that enable agents to decompose complex goals into actionable plans, execute multi-step reasoning, and adapt plans based on feedback. Covers classical planning (STRIPS, PDDL), LLM-based planning (zero-shot, few-shot), recursive task decomposition, Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) for agents, backtracking and replanning, hierarchical task networks (HTN), and temporal reasoning. Includes planning under uncertainty.
column5: STRIPS, PDDL, Task Decomposition, MCTS, HTN, Backtracking, Replanning, Temporal Reasoning, Goal Regression, Subgoal Management

column4: The mechanisms by which agents discover, select, and execute external tools to extend their capabilities beyond text generation. Covers three integration patterns: Direct API calls, Function/Tool Calling (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google), and Model Context Protocol (MCP). Includes tool registries, dynamic tool discovery, parallel tool calls, tool schemas (JSON Schema), error handling for tool failures, sandboxed execution, and the Agent-as-Tool recursive pattern.
column5: MCP, Function Calling, JSON Schema, Tool Registry, Parallel Calls, OpenAI Agents SDK, Claude Agent SDK, Sandboxed Execution, Code Interpreter

column4: The architecture pattern that enhances LLM outputs by retrieving relevant external information before generation. Covers traditional RAG (chunking, embedding, vector search), advanced RAG (query rewriting, reranking, hybrid search), agentic RAG (agents that actively investigate rather than simply retrieve), self-RAG (agents that evaluate whether retrieval is needed), and corrective RAG. Includes document processing, embedding strategies, and evaluation metrics.
column5: Chunking Strategies, Embeddings, Vector Search, Query Rewriting, Reranking (Cohere), Agentic RAG, Self-RAG, Corrective RAG, Hybrid Search, Contextual Compression

column4: The application of agentic AI to automate complex, multi-step business and technical workflows. Covers event-driven architectures, scheduled agent execution, pipeline orchestration, integration with existing enterprise systems (ERP, CRM, BPM), document processing workflows, approval chains, exception handling, and long-running workflow persistence. Includes agent-triggered automation vs. human-initiated agent assistance.
column5: Event-Driven Architecture, Celery, Temporal.io, Apache Airflow, BPM Integration, Document Processing, Approval Chains, Long-Running Workflows

column4: The compute, storage, networking, and operational infrastructure required to run agentic AI systems in production. Covers the five infrastructure layers: Compute (serverless, containers, VMs), Storage (vector DBs, Redis, PostgreSQL), Communication (REST, WebSockets, message queues), Observability, and Security. Includes deployment patterns (blue-green, shadow, canary), scaling strategies, cold start optimization, and cost management.
column5: Kubernetes, Docker, AWS Lambda, Redis, Pinecone, CI/CD for Agents, Blue-Green Deploy, Canary Releases, Auto-scaling, Cost Optimization

column4: The practices and tools for monitoring, debugging, and evaluating agent behavior in development and production. Covers structured logging of reasoning traces, distributed tracing across multi-agent workflows, token usage and cost tracking, latency metrics, success/failure rates, LangSmith/LangFuse integration, agent-specific evaluation frameworks (LLM-as-judge), benchmark suites (BFCL, SWE-bench), regression testing, A/B testing for prompts, and feedback loops.
column5: LangSmith, LangFuse, Distributed Tracing, LLM-as-Judge, BFCL, SWE-bench, Regression Testing, A/B Testing, Feedback Loops, Reasoning Trace Logging

column4: The frameworks and controls for ensuring agentic AI systems operate within defined boundaries and do not cause harm. Covers three boundary layers: Goal boundaries, Tool access boundaries, Output boundaries. Includes prompt injection defense, output filtering, data redaction, RBAC for agents, audit trails, compliance (GDPR, SOC2), AI governance frameworks, kill switches, rate limiting, adversarial testing, and responsible AI principles. Addresses the finding that 82% of implementations have security vulnerabilities.
column5: Prompt Injection Defense, RBAC, Audit Trails, Guardrails, Kill Switches, Adversarial Testing, GDPR Compliance, Responsible AI, Output Filtering, Rate Limiting

column4: The integration of all domains into reliable, scalable, maintainable agent systems that operate continuously in production environments. Covers system design principles (modularity, observability, HITL governance, adaptive feedback), fault tolerance and graceful degradation, session management, versioning (prompts, tools, agents), disaster recovery, cost management strategies, performance optimization, and the complete agent lifecycle from prototype to production. Addresses why 40% of agentic AI projects are projected to be scrapped by 2027.
